title: When did the two species split?
hook: Two species differ at 1.2% of their DNA letters. How long ago did they split?

knows: DNA differences accumulate over time as mutations
doesNotKnow: that the difference between two species builds up along both lines since they split

misconception: Two species differing by 1.2% split when one line gained 1.2%.
objective: The learner can explain that the difference between two species is the changes on both branches, 2 x rate x time, so 1.2% at 0.1% per line per million years means a split 6 million years ago, not 12.

claims.text: After two species split, each lineage accumulates changes independently, so the difference between them is about 2 x rate x time since the split.
claims.source: Zuckerkandl & Pauling, Evolving Genes and Proteins, 1965 (molecular clock); Graur & Li, Fundamentals of Molecular Evolution, 2000, divergence d = 2rt.

claims.text: With a difference of 1.2% and a rate of 0.1% per million years on each line, the split was 1.2 / (2 x 0.1) = 6 million years ago; splits 3 and 12 million years ago would give 0.6% and 2.4%.
claims.source: Arithmetic; Demo.tsx diff(t) = 2 x t tenths of a percent. 3 gives 0.6%, 6 gives 1.2%, 9 gives 1.8%, 12 gives 2.4%.

claims.text: Model (stated on the stage): the rate of 0.1% per million years is made up; the toy clock assumes a constant rate and no letter changing twice.
claims.source: Model choice in Demo.tsx; brief life #46. Real rates vary by gene and lineage, and repeat hits at the same site make older differences undercounted (Graur & Li 2000).

recall.question: Two species differ at 3% of their DNA letters, and each line changes at 0.1% per million years. About when did they split?
recall.why: The 3% builds up on both branches, so each line gained 1.5%; at 0.1% per million years that is 15 million years.
